overlap.title: Overlap damages both content and attribution.
overlap.description: Within-recording penalty for utterances with at least 50% overlap exposure versus non-overlapped utterances.
overlap.note: All reported overlap penalties are statistically significant.

similarity.title: Similar voices are consistently confused.
similarity.description: Spearman correlation between pairwise voice similarity and directional speaker confusion on non-overlapping speech.
similarity.note: All seven correlations are positive and significant (p < 0.05).

acoustic.title: Poor acoustics primarily affect lexical recognition.
acoustic.description: Correlation with acoustic difficulty on utterances away from overlap and speaker-turn boundaries.
acoustic.note: Lexical correlations are significant for all systems; attribution effects are weak and inconsistent.

turn.title: Speaker transitions mainly disrupt who spoke.
turn.description: Attribution penalty near non-overlapping speaker switches using a ±0.5 s boundary neighborhood.
turn.note: The attribution penalty is significant for every evaluated system; lexical penalties are not consistently significant.

speaker.title: More speakers are associated with attribution difficulty.
speaker.description: Speaker-count association after controlling for dataset identity and overlap; P3 is excluded to reduce source-specific bias.
speaker.note: Controlled analysis—not a raw P0→P3 trend. SoulX-Transcriber is excluded because its 5-minute units do not always contain every recording-level speaker.
